newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs to hold steady, EMU worries to fade.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs to hold steady, EMU worries to fade.

text.p: Belgian government bonds (OLOs) and futures are expected to hold steady in coming days as the focus shifts away from concern about the future of EMU and the euro and towards economic fundamentals, dealers said on Tuesday.

"Belgian 10-year yields could fall to 5.90 or 5.80 percent," analyst Conrad Fieremans at Kredietbank said, before data from the U.S. and Germany, expected to give evidence of economic strength, would take them back to around six percent.
The benchmark yield BE286= was at 5.91 percent in late trade, down from 6.00 percent on Monday. Its outperformance against Bunds pushed the spread down to eight bps from nine.

Analysts said players were shifting to the view that it was better for EMU to start, and the euro to possibly be weaker than intended in the Maastricht Treaty, than for the project to be delayed, possibly indefinitely, because the Maastricht criteria were too tough and could not be met, even by what are seen as the founding members - France and Germany.

"The EMU risk premium decreased today," another analyst said. Pro-EMU comments from France's ruling Socialists FR-EMU and indications that a row between Bonn and the Bundesbank over the use of central bank gold reserves to state finances DE-EMU was coming to an end had provided support.
The analyst said reduced concern about a failure of EMU had removed fears about an impending safe-haven move into Treasuries. Nevertheless, Treasuries remained strong, heading

A lack of selling pressure also underpinned OLOs. "OLO holders do not want to go short, certainly not after the strength of recent days (in the face of the recent French Left's election victory and the row in Germany)," a trader said.
Fieremans at Kredietbank expected likely news of economic strength in Germany and the U.S. to keep a lid on the market. German output and orders numbers are due this week.

Germany's economy is expected to show greater strength in the first quarter than in the preceding quarter despite continued worries about the labour and construction markets, economists said. The long-awaited upswing could also start finally to translate into shorter dole queues when labour market figures for May are released on Friday DE-ECI.

The expected pickup would translate into higher official rates, in Germany but also in Belgium, later this year or early next year, Fieremans said. Markets had not yet discounted this, which was reflected by the meagre 20 basis point spread between June and March BIBOR futures O#BIB:.
